papers.title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity
papers.abstract: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. We investigate equatorial motion around the non-singular Schwarzschild black hole of conformal gravity, in which the conformal scale \(L\) removes the curvature divergence at the origin while preserving the event horizon at \(r=2M\) and recovering the Schwarzschild geometry as \(L\to 0\). Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the conserved energy and angular momentum in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime and construct the radial effective potential for spinning particles. This allows us to determine the physical timelike spin bound, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the degeneracy between \(L\) and the Kerr rotation parameter, and representative bound trajectories. We show that \(L\) strengthens the effective-potential barrier, decreases the ISCO radius, angular momentum and energy, and lowers the maximum admissible spin before the trajectory becomes spacelike. The orbital integrations reveal a clear division of roles: \(L\) governs the compactness of the bound orbit, whereas the particle spin governs the accumulated relativistic precession. These results establish spinning-particle dynamics as a sensitive diagnostic of conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and provide a possible route to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from standard Schwarzschild background.

papers.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
papers.abstract: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.

papers.title: Extracting Energy from a Traversable Wormhole via Magnetic Reconnection: Circular Orbits and the Plunging Region
papers.abstract: Using the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism, we study energy extraction from the Teo traversable rotating wormhole at different orbital locations. This wormhole has no event horizon and cannot reduce to a Kerr black hole in any parameter limit. We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. Compared with a Kerr black hole under the same plasma parameters, the Teo wormhole has higher energy extraction power and efficiency. This is completely different from the Simpson-Visser rotating wormhole, which can reduce to a Kerr black hole, where the large spin makes efficiency and power decrease. We also extend magnetic reconnection to the plunging region. We find that when the spin is not particularly high, the energy extraction power and efficiency in the plunging region are higher than those in the circular orbit region, while for very high spin the situation is reversed. This conclusion also differs from that obtained from a Kerr black hole, where the power and efficiency in the plunging region are always higher than those in the circular orbit region.

papers.title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
papers.abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes gravitational waves of different momenta travel different distances during the same cosmic interval. A relic stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a finite momentum bandwidth therefore samples a shell of finite thickness, rather than the thin source shell of massless propagation from a single epoch. We describe this effective last-scattering surface by mapping the momentum and emission-time distribution into a radial visibility window in an FLRW background. The calculation uses the geometric-optics propagation relation and includes both dispersion and finite emission duration, without a small-mass or narrow-band approximation. We then calculate how radial averaging changes the angular power for an early-produced background whose momentum channels trace a common source-fluctuation field. For a scale-invariant source spectrum, moving a thin shell leaves its angular power unchanged, so the reduction in power isolates the effect of its finite thickness. For a logarithmic momentum width of $0.5$, mass-to-momentum ratios $q=0.3,1,3$ give angular-power ratios of approximately $0.974$, $0.771$, and $0.508$ at $\ell=10$. At a representative frequency of $3\,\mathrm{nHz}$, these ratios correspond to masses of approximately $3.6\times10^{-24}$--$1.2\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$. We establish a framework that maps the graviton mass to the SGWB angular power spectrum through its effect on propagation distances and the radial window, for a specified source distribution and frequency selection. Using this framework for graviton-mass inference requires a source and detector model; the calculation here establishes the angular response rather than an observational sensitivity.

papers.title: Degenerate wormhole as a topological oscillator
papers.abstract: A spherically symmetric, matter free degenerate wormhole is considered as a gravitational system with a single collective degree of freedom, the radius of its throat. The classical dynamics is determined by applying the equivalence principle to the motion of the throat, while canonical quantization reduces the dynamics to a spectral problem with the dynamical symmetry group \(SU(1,1)\). The exact solution of this spectral problem reveals two qualitatively different regimes. For subPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits Bohr type states characterized by a gravitational Bohr radius \(\hbar^2/(GM^3)\). For superPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits a semiclassical regime represented by the Einstein Rosen wormhole with Schwarzschild gravitational radius \(2GM/c^2\). Thus, the model connects the familiar quantum bound state behavior with the semiclassical geometry of a gravitational horizon.

papers.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the exponential accumulation of successive disk images. We construct images of an opaque thermal disk and a transparent emitting sheet, taking into account gravitational frequency shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity. Positive $q$ increases the local thermal emission and accelerates the accumulation of successive images around the common critical curve. Under the universal coupling assumptions associated with the quoted Solar System bounds, the fractional corrections are of order $10^{-11}$ in flux and $10^{-12}$ in temperature.

papers.title: Damour--Solodukhin Wormholes: Matter Sources, Observational Constraints, and Accretion Dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the physical realization and observational properties of Damour--Solodukhin wormholes within general relativity. We first construct an explicit matter source supporting this geometry, consisting of a phantom scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, and examine both electric and magnetic configurations. We then study the propagation of photons and derive constraints on the wormhole deformation parameter $\lambda$ using Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*. We show that, for $\lambda^2 \leq 1/2$, the shadow radius coincides exactly with the Schwarzschild value, although the radial geometry continues to affect gravitational lensing and the structure of photon rings. Using a thin accretion disk with a Johnson SU emissivity profile, we investigate the resulting optical images and examine the effects of the wormhole throat on their structure. Finally, we analyze stationary relativistic accretion and demonstrate that, for identical boundary conditions, the energy density and particle number density are independent of $\lambda$ throughout the common exterior region, while the radial velocity retains an explicit dependence on the deformation parameter. We also derive the condition $0 < w < (1+4\lambda^2)^{-1}$ for the existence of an exterior sonic point. These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.

papers.title: Analysis of a Core Envelope Model for PSR J1614-2230 in $f(R)= R+αR^{2} +γR^{3}$ gravity and Tidal Deformability
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the tidal deformability of an anisotropic core-envelope model for the compact star PSR J1614-2230 within the framework of modified f(R) gravity. The stellar interior is divided into two regions, with the core described by a linear equation of state (EoS) and the envelope by a quadratic EoS. The Tolman VII form is adopted for the radial metric potential in both regions. The interior solutions are matched at the core-envelope interface and to the exterior Schwarzschild spacetime through the appropriate junction conditions. The tidal Love number is determined by solving the coupled perturbation equations for the scalar field. The resulting configuration is free from singularities and satisfies the energy conditions, causality requirements, adiabatic index constraint, Herrera cracking condition, and hydrostatic equilibrium condition. The predicted tidal deformability is consistent with the constraints from GW170817, supporting the physical viability of the proposed core-envelope configuration in cubic f(R) gravity.

papers.title: Photon sphere, shadow, and polarized images of thick accretion flows around a quantum Lee-Wick black hole
papers.abstract: We study the optical appearance of a static, spherically symmetric black hole (BH) in sixth-derivative Lee-Wick gravity with an exponential coupling S1 and an oscillatory coupling S2. From the null-geodesic effective potential we derive the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and shadow radius. In the weak-coupling (Block-1) regime the shadow radius rapidly approaches the Schwarzschild value 3 sqrt(3) M, while in the strong-coupling (Block-2) regime the interplay of exponential damping and oscillatory modulation yields non-monotonic and, in some regions, strongly suppressed shadows. We classify the (S1, S2) plane by the number of horizons and unstable photon spheres: horizonless configurations retain a critical curve but lack a central brightness depression, and configurations with two unstable photon spheres show a shadow bounded by the inner one plus an outer photon ring. The 1-sigma/2-sigma EHT bounds for M87* and Sgr A* exclude certain strong-coupling bands. We develop a ray-tracing code that integrates exact Lee-Wick null geodesics, computes 230 GHz thermal-synchrotron emission from a geometrically thick, optically thin RIAF-like flow, and transports linear polarization via the Walker-Penrose constants. Compared with Schwarzschild, in the strong-coupling regime the beam-convolved ring diameter deviates by up to ~14%, the photon-ring Lyapunov exponent grows from pi to about 4-9, and the beta_2 amplitude rises by up to ~50% for a radial-toroidal field, while the phase of beta_2 is nearly insensitive to (S1, S2) at low inclination, mainly tracing the field geometry. A parametrized shock-cone model, motivated by earlier Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton simulations, shows that shock structures modulate the flux in a viewing-azimuth-dependent way without changing the critical-curve size. These are the first shadow, thick-disk, and polarized synthetic images of the Lee-Wick BH.

papers.title: Traversable wormholes from entropy-corrected holographic dark energy with quasinormal mode stability in $f(R,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) motivated energy density profiles as viable matter sources for the construction of traversable wormholes in the framework of $f(R,T)$ gravity. Wormhole solutions are developed using entropy-corrected HDE models based on the Bekenstein--Hawking, Rényi, and Moradpour formalisms. We derive the corresponding shape functions and analyze the influence of the model parameters on the flare-out conditions, obtaining the parameter bounds required for traversability. The null energy condition is examined under these constraints and is found to be violated near the wormhole throat, thereby providing the exotic matter content necessary to sustain the geometry. We further evaluate the total gravitational energy and the complexity factor, showing that the internal structure of the wormhole spacetime is highly sensitive to the underlying entropy prescription. The regularity of the solutions is tested through curvature invariants, confirming the absence of curvature singularities and the asymptotic decay of the Kretschmann scalar. In addition, the generalized Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equation is used to study hydrostatic equilibrium, where the inward hydrostatic force is balanced by the anisotropic force and the extra force induced by the matter--geometry coupling. Finally, scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal modes are computed using the third-order WKB approximation. The negative imaginary parts of all obtained frequencies indicate damped oscillations and hence perturbative stability of the wormhole configurations. Our results show that entropy-corrected HDE models, particularly the Rényi and Moradpour cases, significantly affect the curvature profile, structural complexity, equilibrium behavior, and ringdown response of traversable wormholes in modified $f(R,T)$ gravity.

papers.title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
papers.abstract: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $\rho+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8\pi L^2(\rho+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.

papers.title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
papers.abstract: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < \lambda < 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: Gyromagnetic ratios of slowly rotating charged Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes, supported by a phantom scalar field in Einstein--Maxwell theory, connect two asymptotically flat regions, so a rotating member carries a magnetic dipole moment and a gyromagnetic ratio at each mouth. We construct the slowly rotating family in closed form on all three background branches and show that, within the stationary axial dipole sector and with no applied magnetic field, the first-order solution is unique. The two gyromagnetic ratios obey an exact deficit relation set by the static geometry alone. It gives $g_\pm<2$ at both mouths, bounds the deficit by two-thirds of the squared ratio of scalar to electric charge, and, through the positivity of the reduced magnetic moment, gives each ratio the sign of the mass of its own mouth; the two ratios coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats, so their difference measures the asymmetry of the wormhole. Rotation drags the two ends relative to each other in a definite sense, with a dragging profile that decreases monotonically across the throat, and the electromagnetic field carries a strictly positive share of the angular momentum on every finite sphere. Toward the extremal edge at the positive mouth the deficit closes cubically on every trajectory studied, because the redshift factor at the throat vanishes quadratically; the coefficient depends on the path. When the charge is switched off, the frame dragging reproduces known neutral results, whereas on the massive neutral branch the gyromagnetic ratios stay away from the Kerr--Newman value.

papers.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
papers.abstract: The Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($\chi^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $\chi^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

papers.title: Eos: a merger-induced starburst at the dawn of Galactic low-$α$ disc formation
papers.abstract: The last significant merger of the Milky Way, the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GS/E), is thought to have reshaped the early Galaxy and to mark the transition from the high-$\alpha$ to the low-$\alpha$ disc. The stars formed in situ during this merger offer a direct record of that epoch but are hard to identify. Using APOGEE DR17 abundances, we study Eos, a population of in-situ low-$\alpha$ stars on halo-like, non-rotating, eccentric orbits. The metal-poor part of Eos has a nitrogen dispersion as large as that of the pre-disc Aurora population and up to 1.7 times that of the low-$\alpha$ disc at the same metallicity. Heating alone cannot produce this: the Splash, a disc heated onto halo orbits by the same merger and selected in the same way, shows no excess over its parent disc. This part of Eos was therefore born in poorly mixed gas. Eos is also chemically intermediate between the accreted GS/E debris and the coeval in-situ Milky Way stars, and stars with more GS/E-like chemistry move on more extended orbits. Its stars are older than the bulk of the low-$\alpha$ disc but younger than the high-$\alpha$ disc and the Splash. We compare these observations with a merger-induced starburst seen in an Auriga simulation. There, a GS/E-like merger funnels the stripped progenitor gas into a mixing lane of intermediate metallicity, where stars form with intermediate abundances, a large chemical dispersion and a chemodynamical gradient set by their birth site, reproducing the observed signatures of Eos. We therefore interpret Eos as the surviving relic of the GS/E merger-induced starburst, born largely from the partially mixed gas bridging the two galaxies and marking the onset of the Milky Way's low-$\alpha$ disc. Eos thus provides a direct observational view of the star formation and galaxy evolution driven by the Milky Way's last significant merger.

papers.title: Top-heavy Initial Mass Functions are not enough at cosmic dawn
papers.abstract: A top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) has been proposed to explain the unexpected abundance of ultraviolet (UV)-bright galaxies at cosmic dawn. We test this possibility using the metallicity-dependent, top-heavy IMF recently proposed by Chon et al. (2024), which is motivated by simulations of metal-poor star formation. We compare this IMF with a Salpeter IMF, self-consistently including the associated changes in UV emission, supernova feedback, metal enrichment, and dust production. At fixed star formation rate, the Chon IMF enhances the intrinsic UV luminosity by a factor ${B}_{1500}\simeq4.7$-$2.8$ over halo masses $M_h=10^{8-12}\,M_\odot$. However, its larger supernova rate suppresses star formation and increases dust attenuation, reducing the net boost to ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq2.0$-$1.06$. For halos relevant to the bright end of the UV luminosity function, the enhancement is only ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq1.2$-$1.4$, or about $0.3$ mag. Calculations with the DELPHI semi-analytic model confirm that the self-consistent Chon and Salpeter UV luminosity functions differ by less than $0.5$ dex at $z\simeq11$-$17$. Thus, a top-heavy IMF alone cannot explain the bright galaxy excess. Conversely, the predicted pair-instability supernova abundance differs by factors of $2$-$6$ between the two IMFs, providing a potentially cleaner observational diagnostic of the high-mass stellar populations at these early epochs.

papers.title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
papers.abstract: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$\Delta_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$\gamma$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $\gamma$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $\delta\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $\delta\ell$.

papers.title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
papers.abstract: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

papers.title: Influence of variable IMF on the dynamical black hole mass estimates in massive ETGs
papers.abstract: Several studies have shown that the stellar initial mass function (IMF) in massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) is not universal. Recent results from stellar population synthesis models, based on integral-field unit (IFU) observations, indicate that the IMF varies radially, becoming increasingly bottom-heavy towards galaxy centres. This radial variation alters the stellar mass-to-light ratio ($\rm M_{*}/L$) and can significantly affect dynamical black hole (BH) mass estimates in massive ETGs. In this study, we investigate the impact of a radially varying IMF on BH mass estimates for five massive galaxies: NGC3923, NGC4261, NGC4636, IC4296, and IC4329. Using DYNAMITE, a triaxial Schwarzschild orbit-based modelling code, we perform mass modelling of these galaxies based on MUSE and SINFONI IFU observations. Our models incorporate radially varying stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ profiles derived from spatially resolved stellar population modelling with a free IMF, and we compare the resulting BH masses with those obtained from dynamical models assuming a constant stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$. All galaxies in our sample show bottom-heavy IMFs in their central regions, with the IMF generally becoming lighter towards larger radii. We obtain constrained BH masses for NGC3923 and IC4329, while only upper limits are obtained for NGC4261, NGC4636, and IC4296. Compared with the constant-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models, the variable-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models yield BH masses lower by approximately 83% and 11% for NGC3923 and IC4329, respectively, while the BH mass upper limits for the other galaxies can increase or decrease. Our results demonstrate that spatial variations in the IMF and stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ can have a non-negligible but strongly galaxy-dependent impact on dynamical BH mass measurements. These results highlight the importance of accounting for such variations in future dynamical modelling efforts.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

papers.title: Twisted resonant orbits: Quantifying the deceleration of the Galactic bar
papers.abstract: Recent structural discoveries in Gaia Data Release 3 reveal distinct, chevron-shaped over-densities in the radial phase space of the halo. Although initial interpretations identify these features as the phase-mixed relics of a past galaxy merger, their prominent asymmetry and persistence at high metallicities strongly challenge this interpretation. These features are better explained as a dynamical response to a Galactic bar, where stars are trapped in resonances. We establish the fractional $v_r$ asymmetry of the chevrons as a quantitative diagnostic tool for the bar's rotational state. We utilise test-particle simulations of a Milky Way-like galaxy to model various bar pattern speed evolutions, including decelerating and constant speed scenarios. By mapping the fractional asymmetry of the phase-space chevrons across a parameter space of bar deceleration rates and pattern speeds, we establish a direct correlation between the bar's deceleration and the rotational response of the resonant orbits. Comparing these simulated constraints with observational data from Gaia DR3 provides a framework for measuring the current deceleration of the Galactic bar, and a probe of the amount of dynamical friction occurring between the baryonic and dark matter content of the Milky Way. We find a dimensionless deceleration parameter $\eta \equiv - \dot{\Omega}_b/\Omega_b^2 = 0.0015^{+0.0016}_{-0.0009}$, equivalent to $\dot{\Omega}_b = -2.23^{+1.50}_{-2.46} \, \text{km s}^{-1} \text{kpc}^{-1} \text{Gyr}^{-1}$, in agreement with previous estimates obtained with independent methods. Gaia DR4 should sharpen this measurement considerably.

papers.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

papers.title: Ram Pressure Is Unable to Strip All Phases of the Interstellar Medium out of Spirals Falling into Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: Following the expansion of the Universe, spiral galaxies may fall at large speeds into galaxy clusters. Their interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM) may remove part of their gas and reduce their capacity for making new stars, as envisaged by Gunn & Gott. Ram pressure stripping (RPS) is commonly invoked to explain this gas loss and the wakes or tails left behind in-falling galaxies. Here we revise the impact of RPS on individual dense clouds and particularly focus on turbulent viscous stripping (TVS), driven by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities at the cloud-ICM interface, that affects the high-density and low-temperature molecular gas. For an extended gaseous body to decelerate, momentum from its exposed surface must be communicated into the gas by a hydrodynamic disturbance able to propagate through it. Three-dimensional hydrodynamic calculations follow this interaction with dense clouds. At cloud number densities $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^2$ cm$^{-3}$, ram pressure acting through the transmitted shock strongly compresses and deforms the cloud and produces only a small deceleration; at $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^3$ cm$^{-3}$, the slower transmitted shock produces much weaker deformation. At both cloud densities, TVS continuously removes gas from the cloud surface and forms qualitatively indistinguishable trailing wakes, with comparable mass-loss rates, suggesting that TVS acting on individual dense clouds can generate filamentary substructure within jellyfish-galaxy tails.

papers.title: Kinetic Tomography with Diffuse Interstellar Bands in APOGEE DR17
papers.abstract: Context: Mapping gas flows in the interstellar medium is key to understanding the formation of structure in our Milky Way. Methods that simultaneously reconstruct clouds' distances and line-of-sight velocities are called kinetic tomography (KT). Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are powerful tracers for such maps because they trace the integrated dust density and the dust-weighted velocity. Previous DIB-KT works had small samples with coarse kpc-scale resolution and could not capture vertical disk structure. Aims: Make 4D (3D position + radial velocity) maps of the Milky Way from new, high-quality 15,273 Å DIB detections in APOGEE DR17. Methods: We combine variational inference and Gaussian processes with a mixture likelihood for low signal-to-noise detections and marginalization over distance uncertainties. We calibrate the model on mock fields and spectral injection tests and validate the map against independent tracers of the dust density (3D dust maps) and velocity substructure (masers and young stellar clusters). Results: We recover a posterior distribution over 3D maps of the density and velocity structure of the 15,273 Å DIB within 6 kpc of the Sun. We measure the large-scale structure of the DIB disk (scale length, height and flare) and detect vertical distortions consistent with the warp. On smaller scales, the map resolves distance ambiguities in gas longitude-velocity diagrams. From the second-order velocity structure function, we measure a slope (0.64 $\pm$ 0.04) consistent with Kolmogorov turbulence, amplitude consistent with expectations for molecular clouds, and a preliminary ratio of compressive-to-solenoidal modes. Conclusions: With larger DIB catalogs expected from SDSS-V, this framework should resolve kinematic substructure at the scales needed to constrain the formation and dynamics of individual clouds and voids. papers.title: Off-Nuclear AGN Signatures in MaNGA: Spatially resolved selection using MEGACUBES
papers.abstract: We present a spatially resolved search for off-nuclear active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidates in the MaNGA survey. Using megacubes, we analyze over 10,000 galaxies, separating AGN activity from diffuse ionized gas with refined equivalent-width and surface-brightness thresholds. Combining a spatial radial algorithm with BPT, WHaN, and WHaD diagnostics, we classify 261 nuclear AGNs, 201 off-nuclear AGNs, and 159 'quiet' (composite-spaxel-dominated) sources. We test whether off-nuclear AGNs reside in distinct host galaxies or whether the offset is a local, gas-driven phenomenon. Nuclear and off-nuclear AGN hosts are statistically indistinguishable in stellar mass, age, star formation rate, and gas-phase metallicity. However, the excitation and kinematics of the AGN-ionized gas differ significantly: nuclear AGN spaxels have [O III]$\lambda5007$ luminosities $\sim 0.7$ dex higher than off-nuclear spaxels, whose lower [O III]/H$\beta$ ratios indicate genuinely lower-excitation gas rather than an obscured view of the central engine. We also find an orientation trend: 72% of nuclear hosts are face-on, versus 50% of off-nuclear hosts, so projection effects contribute to, but do not fully explain, off-nuclear detections. The classical WHaN boundary at $\log$([N II]/H$\alpha$) = -0.4 misclassifies high-metallicity diffuse ionized gas in integral field data; an empirical shift to -0.25 removes over 48,000 spurious AGN spaxels. Finally, the off-nuclear fraction implies an episodic AGN phase lifetime of $\sim 5 \times 10^4$ yr, consistent within a factor of a few with independent fading-AGN estimates and supporting short, recurrent accretion bursts.

papers.title: Revealing galaxy assembly bias with luminosity-weighted marked correlations
papers.abstract: We investigate whether luminosity-weighted marked correlation functions can reveal secondary halo information beyond that encoded by halo mass alone, as expected in scenarios of galaxy assembly bias. We propose a controlled null test in which galaxy luminosities follow the same mean luminosity--halo mass relation and scatter, while their residuals are either (A) uncorrelated with secondary halo properties or (B) correlated with a standardized secondary halo property, $s$. Both models have identical halo occupation, galaxy positions, luminosity function, and unweighted projected two-point correlation function, $w_p(r_p)$, so their distinction is encoded entirely in the luminosity marks. At leading order, the projected marked correlation function difference, $\Delta\mathcal{M}_p(r_p)$, scales as $\rho^2\sigma_{\log L}^2\xi_{ss}(r_p)$, where $\rho$ controls the coupling between the luminosity and secondary-property residuals, $\sigma_{\log L}$ is the scatter in log luminosity at fixed halo mass, and $\xi_{ss}$ describes the spatial correlation of the secondary property. We test this framework using a DESI-BGS mock catalogue over $0.1<z<0.4$. For the injected dependence, we detect a marked-clustering deviation over $0.11<r_p/(h^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc})<1.04$, obtaining $\chi^2=30.14$ relative to the null covariance. A one-parameter test rejects the mass-only hypothesis at greater than $5\sigma$ significance ($p=2.13\times10^{-7}$) for $|\rho|>0.63$. At fixed $\sigma_{\log L}=0.23$, correlations as weak as $|\rho|\simeq0.52$ remain detectable, with the results stable under variations in the HOD prescription and modelled galaxy selection effects. These results establish luminosity-weighted marked clustering as a sensitive null test for property-based galaxy assembly bias and secondary halo information hidden from unweighted two-point clustering.

papers.title: A novel pathway to stellar-mass black hole growth: Re-accretion of gas from stellar wind bubbles
papers.abstract: The formation of high-mass stellar black holes (BHs) observed in mergers by gravitational wave observatories remains difficult to explain using standard models of stellar evolution. We investigate whether newly formed stellar-mass BHs in dense molecular clouds can significantly increase their final mass by accreting gas from pre-existing, wind-blown interstellar bubbles produced by their progenitor stars. We performed 1D and 3D hydrodynamic simulations of interstellar bubbles driven by stellar feedback, incorporating thermal conduction, radiative cooling, gravity, ionizing radiation, stellar winds, and supernova (SN) explosions. We modeled the subsequent accretion onto the central BH for two formation scenarios: core-collapse SN and direct collapse. Our parameter space study encompasses over 500 1D simulations, varying initial cloud densities, gravitational binding energies, progenitor masses ($40-257\,M_\odot$), and metallicities ($0.66\,Z_\odot$ and $0.016\,Z_\odot$), and tracks the bubble evolution for millions of years post-BH formation. Scenarios exhibiting significant re-accretion were further validated using high-resolution 3D simulations. Our simulations show that BHs formed via direct collapse from low-metallicity progenitors can accrete up to $6.9\,M_\odot$ of gas from massive inner shells formed by late-stage slow winds, resulting in final BH masses of up to $93\,M_\odot$. Conversely, we find no significant re-accretion in scenarios involving an SN explosion or high-metallicity progenitors; in these cases, fast winds or SN ejecta efficiently evacuate dense structures from the bubble interior, leaving behind a hot, low-density medium. [abridged] This mechanism may help explain the unexpectedly high masses of BHs observed in gravitational wave events.

papers.title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $\alpha_I^3/\kappa$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_\phi$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff. For an instantaneous quadratic state initialized at the bounce, the equilateral cubic diagnostic first reaches unity at $K\simeq0.6483m_{\rm P}$. Evolution over $0\le t/t_{\rm P}\le10$ lowers this crossing to $K\simeq0.64626m_{\rm P}$. Sampled shape and independent frequency-assignment tests do not lower these thresholds. A fourth-order adiabatic ultraviolet tail can be attached without changing the tested finite modes. These results identify pre-bounce nonlinear enhancement and a candidate bounce-state window. Broader evolution and shape tests, renormalized backreaction, observational mode mapping on a consistently normalized background, and a complete fourth-order theory remain necessary to establish interacting consistency.

papers.title: Multiphase Gas in High-$z$ Cosmic Sheets
papers.abstract: We present high-resolution cosmological simulations of individual cosmic sheets ($z=3-6$) using the moving-mesh code AREPO to study cold gas ($T\approx10^4\rm ~K$) in the diffuse cosmic web. We find cosmic sheet gas forms a fragmented morphology, evident as kiloparsec-scale variations in the neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm HI}$). Fragmentation arises from the bending and disruption of the cold-dense sheet core into a multiphase medium. Nonlinear thin shell instability (NTSI) and later shear-induced vorticity drive this bending, rather than previously suggested thermal or Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities. Higher resolution enhances fragmentation. Across a fourfold range in spatial resolution, $N_{\rm HI}$ covering fractions increase by factors of $\approx 1.5-3.5$ for partial Lyman-limit systems (pLLS) and Lyman-limit systems (LLS). An order-of-magnitude estimate suggests sheets may host a large fraction of the ultra-low metallicity (p)LLS population. Equivalent MP-Gadget simulations show qualitatively similar fragmentation, but numerical smoothing effects are present. Cosmic-sheet gas properties remain unconverged despite our high resolutions.

papers.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $\Omega_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $\Omega_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $\Omega_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $\Omega_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

papers.title: Design and Forecasts for a Rubin Twilight Program for Nearby Type Ia Supernovae
papers.abstract: Nearby Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are important for supernova cosmology, but saturation in 30 s exposures, gaps in light-curve sampling, and the footprint of Vera C. Rubin Observatory's baseline Wide-Fast-Deep (WFD) survey limit the nearby sample. For measurements of structure growth at $0.02 \le z<0.06$, the fractional uncertainty on $f\sigma_8$ decreases from 0.783 to 0.305. Restricting the program to $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -11^\circ$ reduces the dark-energy improvement to 7.2%. These short exposures could also provide unsaturated photometry of potential distance-ladder calibrators at $z<0.02$.

papers.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$\alpha$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

papers.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
papers.abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

papers.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: In the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case. For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.

papers.title: Thermodynamic topology and orbital dynamics of charged RN--AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract: This study investigates the topological thermodynamic properties and orbital dynamics of the Reissner--Nordström anti-de Sitter (RN--AdS) black hole with logarithmic corrections solution in Einstein--Maxwell gravity. By utilizing the Duan's $\Phi$-mapping theory, we investigate the topological classes within the generalized three-parameter Sharma--Mittal entropy formalism. Employing different thermodynamic ensembles, including the canonical and mixed canonical ensembles, we explore the critical, divergence points and heat capacity, which help us determine the thermodynamic stability of the BH. In addition, the Hamiltonian formalism is employed to investigate the orbital and oscillatory motion of neutral test particles. By utilizing the effective potential approach, we examine the effective force, the stability of circular orbits, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We further analyze the trajectories of test particles and derive the radial $\left(\omega_{r}\right)$, latitudinal $\left(\omega_{\theta}\right)$, and azimuthal $\left(\omega_{\phi}\right)$ oscillation frequencies, together with the periastron precession frequency. This work provides key insights into the fundamental nature of Einstein--Maxwell gravity. Moreover, these results provide a comprehensive theoretical description of the orbital dynamics of the RN--AdS black hole solution and may be useful for future high-precision astrophysical observations.

papers.title: Phase transitions in self-gravitating objects and black holes: Common properties and interpretations
papers.abstract: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. The model consists of a monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ of a Jüttner gas. From the partition function we obtain an exact modified Bessel expression for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ and supply compact Padé approximants with good accuracy across all temperatures. These inputs yield a closed virial-capacity formula, which we use to determine where the heat capacity changes sign as the support pressure becomes competitive with the thermal pressure. We then contrast this behavior with Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes. Despite the disparate microphysics, both systems exhibit a switch in heat-capacity behavior governed by competing pressure contributions. The surrogate model provides compact analytic insight into stability thresholds in self-gravitating systems and their black-hole analogues.

papers.title: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk $-$ new insights from GALAH DR4
papers.abstract: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk has drawn extensive attention since ESA's \textit{Gaia} launch. Complex structure appears across a multi-parameter space of stellar abundances, ages, and kinematics. Using GALAH DR4, we investigate ridge and phase-spiral structures in chemical-abundance, phase ($v_i,x_i$), action--angle ($J_i,\theta_i$), and frequency--action ($\Omega_i,J_i$) spaces ($i=R,\phi,z$). Our sample includes 333,412 disk stars with reliable chemodynamical data. In the $R$--$v_\phi$ plane, ridges trace near-constant $J_\phi$ tracks and show coherent variations in $\theta_R$ and $\theta_\phi$. In $J_\phi$--$J_R$, ridges are most prominent when encoded by $z_{\rm max}$ and preferentially associate with metal-rich, low-$\alpha$ populations. In the solar neighbourhood ($R=7.2$--$9.2$\,kpc), we recover a clear phase spiral in $z$--$v_z$. Encoded in $v_\phi$, $\Omega_R$, or $\Omega_\phi$, one-armed spirals appear, whereas the $v_R$-encoded map shows a two-armed spiral. Projecting actions onto $z$--$v_z$ reveals residual spiral signatures in $J_R$ and $J_\phi$, indicating that the phase spiral encodes in-plane orbital information. Both structures depend on age: ridges remain at similar locations with varying contrast, while the phase spiral is more tightly wound in younger and more loosely wound in older populations. Several ridges correspond in $J_\phi$ to known moving groups, and excluding stars in all six moving-group regions makes the phase spiral less distinct in mean radial velocity maps. These links support interpreting ridges, phase spirals, and moving groups within a common phase-space dynamical framework. Combined with trends in orbital properties, age, and abundance, these findings suggest a common dynamical origin and distinct chemodynamical responses of a perturbed Galactic disk.

papers.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
papers.abstract: We present and analyse the results of Science Data Challenge 3b (SDC3b; this https URL), an Epoch of Reionization (EoR) inference exercise organised by the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) using simulated SKA data. The nine-month challenge, running from October 2024 to May 2025, represents the first community-wide comparison of EoR inference pipelines on common simulated datasets. We consider multiple datasets designed to assess performance on both foreground-free and foreground-contaminated cylindrical power spectra and imaging products, adopting different reionization scenarios and EoR simulation models. We include results from 16 teams, which employ a range of methodologies to infer the posterior distribution of the hydrogen neutral fraction across three redshift intervals spanning z=8.41 to z=6.25. The results show significant inter-team variability of the astrophysical constraints even in the simpler case where only instrumental noise is added to the cosmological signal. This underscores the need for further investigation into the relative contributions of signal modelling, the treatment of instrumental effects, and inference methods to the robustness of the resulting conclusions. Although individual methods can produce biased parameter estimates, the combined average of their estimates remains close to the input values, suggesting that independent approaches can offset method-specific biases.

papers.title: Neutral hydrogen in the Shapley Supercluster core II. Gas content and star formation in the filaments connecting the core
papers.abstract: We investigate the neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) content of galaxies across the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) at z = 0.048 by combining new deep MeerKAT L band observations of five filament pointings with archival MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey observations of the supercluster core. Together with optical data from the Shapley Supercluster Survey, these observations provide a homogeneous view of galaxy evolution from the virialised cluster environment to the surrounding filaments. We compare the HI content, star formation activity, gas depletion timescales, and morphological properties of galaxies relative to the gas fraction and star forming main sequences. The global HI detection fraction increases from 30 per cent in the cluster centre to 45 per cent in the filaments. While HI detected galaxies in the cluster centre are dominated by transition zone systems, the filament population is shared nearly equally between star forming main sequence and transition zone detections, indicating ongoing environmental transformation. Their gas properties also differ: cluster galaxies exhibit progressively depleted HI reservoirs towards the red sequence, whereas filament galaxies remain primarily gas rich. Within the filaments, long HI depletion timescales exceeding the Hubble time are concentrated in specific populations, notably 71 per cent of transition zone and 57 per cent of gas rich detections, indicating the inefficient conversion of atomic gas into stars. The HI detected filament population is dominated by late type galaxies, while the underlying non detected population is primarily composed of early type systems, consistent with environmental pre processing before cluster infall.

papers.title: Magnolia: a highly magnetized galaxy at redshift $z\simeq9$
papers.abstract: The theory of galactic magnetic field growth via dynamo action predicts that the interstellar medium (ISM) of early galaxies would remain virtually unmagnetized on large scales. However, recent observations of strong dust polarization in galaxies at redshifts $z\simeq2.6$ and $z\simeq5.6$ challenge this paradigm. If galaxies indeed host strong, large-scale, coherent magnetic fields at high-$z$, then galaxy evolution and current theories of magnetic field amplification in galaxies should be revisited. To address the full physical complexity of early magnetic field growth in galaxies, we have designed MAGNA SERRA, a suite of radiation-magneto-hydrodynamical (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulations with non-equilibrium chemistry. In this first paper from the MAGNA SERRA suite, we present Magnolia, a galaxy hosted in a $\simeq 10^{11}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ dark matter halo simulated with RAMSES-RT with a $\simeq 10^4~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ mass ($\simeq 10 \,\mathrm{pc}$ spatial) resolution. We find that, at $z\simeq9$, Magnolia has a stellar mass of a few times $10^8~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and is strongly magnetized, reaching a magnetic field of a few $\mu G$ and a plasma beta $\beta\simeq 0.1$ in the densest regions. This strong amplification occurs over a timescale of about 40~Myrs due to the highly dynamical nature of the galaxy, which creates strong compressions and shear. The power spectra of the magnetic and kinetic energies and the spectral energy transfer functions do not suggest dynamo action, but rather an initial magnetic field amplification through a large-scale compression, and a later re-organization of this field from small to large scales. Our findings show that strong galactic magnetization is possible at very high redshifts, which means that magnetic fields can play a dominant role throughout a galaxy's evolutionary history. papers.title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in \(f(R)\) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
papers.abstract: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

papers.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. papers.title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
papers.abstract: In the pure quadratic model of the Böhmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

papers.title: From a mass invariant in a gravo-turbulent medium to the characteristic mass of the star-forming cores
papers.abstract: The origin of the observed universality, or, say, the limited variations, of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and its precursor, the prestellar core mass function (CMF), and thus of the characteristic mass of stars and cores, across a wide range of different galactic environments remains an open, fundamental problem in astrophysics. In this paper, we demonstrate that we can explain this property from gravity and turbulence only, using a mass time-invariant that remains valid for a broad class of turbulent flows throughout the star formation process. This mass invariant is entirely determined by the large-scale normalisation of the field of density fluctuations in the Galactic Interstellar Medium (ISM), induced by turbulence. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we first verify that the temporal invariance of this quantity is preserved in a self-gravitating turbulent medium. Then, introducing a self-consistent model of the statistical properties of the density field in the self-gravitating multiphase turbulent ISM, we show that the universality of the characteristic mass of star-forming cores is imposed by this invariant together with the scaling of the Larson relations. Our model successfully predicts the characteristic mass of the cores in Milky Way-like star-forming regions, as well as in more extreme environments such as high-mass star-forming regions and massive early-type galaxies. This scenario suggests that the characteristic mass of the CMF, and then probably the characteristic stellar mass, originates from a universal, fundamental property of turbulence and is imprinted both by the very early stages of the star formation process in the gravo-turbulent interstellar medium, when the dynamics of the medium are still dominated by turbulence, and by the statistical properties of small-scale self-gravitating structures.

papers.title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $\Lambda$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. papers.title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
papers.abstract: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $\epsilon$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-\epsilon)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

papers.title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
papers.abstract: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. We test the model against cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillations, and Pantheon+ supernova data, with the SH0ES host-distance calibration. Relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM, the data fit improves by $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm data}=-6.90$, or $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm objective}=-3.76$ when Gaussian parameter-prior penalties are included. The scalar-field model gives $H_0=69.53\pm0.26\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, compared with $68.45\pm0.24\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ in flat $\Lambda$CDM. This shift brings the inferred expansion rate closer to the SH0ES measurement, but does not resolve the discrepancy significantly.

papers.title: The Silk Nebula Revisited: A Comment on Wu et al. (2026) and New Constraints from Archival Survey Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Wu et al. (2026) used one LAMOST MRS-N plate to suggest that the Silk Nebula, a $17^\circ$-long \Oiii~$\lambda$5007 filament in Gemini, is possibly associated with a supernova remnant at a fiducial distance of $\sim$160\,pc. We test this against their published values and independent archival data. The \Ni\ airglow in their blue-arm spectrum lies at air, topocentric rest wavelengths, so their \Oiii\ velocities omit the heliocentric correction and are $10.1\pm1.0$\,\kms\ too high. Corrected and combined with DESI DR1 and SDSS spectra, \Oiii\ lies at \vhel\ $=+13.3\pm1.0$\,\kms, the velocity of \Nii\ and of the local warm ionized medium (WIM). Their \Ha\ velocities are 4.5--6.7\,\kms\ redder than \Nii. Their tabulated distances are in kpc, not units of 100\,pc, and kinematic distances carry no information in this direction. Their surface brightness exceeds independent measurements (1.4--2.5 rayleighs) by factors of 4.6--8.6. Their red-line shock criteria are met equally in their nebula-free background region and describe the WIM; their other remnant diagnostics do not constrain the filament. DESI and SDSS spectra show that the filament is Balmer-dark (\Oiii/\Hb\ $>11$) and \Oii-strong, with \ion{He}{2}/\Oiii\ $<0.026$; GALEX shows a coincident ultraviolet ridge, with no \Ha, \ion{H}{1}, dust or X-ray counterpart. These properties, and the lack of an ionizing source, exclude photoionization equilibrium and complete radiative shocks and match a column-truncated radiative shock of $\sim$80--120\,\kms\ seen edge-on, plausibly on the limb of the Monogem Ring at $\sim$250--320\,pc. Far-ultraviolet and deep optical spectroscopy, a two-epoch proper motion and high-ion absorption toward bracketing white dwarfs would be decisive.

papers.title: Disentangling star formation rate indicators in H-ATLAS galaxies: UV, FIR and radio diagnostics from energy-balance SED fitting
papers.abstract: We compare three star formation rate (SFR) tracers --- far-ultraviolet (FUV), far-infrared (FIR) and 1.4\,GHz radio emission --- for \Nsamp\ galaxies (median redshift 0.12) from the Herschel Astrophysical Terahertz Large Area Survey Data Release 1 catalogue, excluding quasars, AGN-dominated galaxies and unreliable redshifts. Energy-balance spectral energy distribution fitting with \textsc{cigale} gives their attenuations, dust luminosities and SFRs self-consistently. The FUV attenuation correlates strongly with FIR luminosity (Spearman $\rho=0.84$), largely through their common dependence on redshift (partial $\rho=0.57$ at fixed $z$), and more tightly with the infrared excess ($\rho=0.96$). The uncorrected UV SFR is over ten times below the FIR SFR for 67 per cent of the galaxies, and for all with $A_{\rm FUV}>4$\,mag. For 714 galaxies the FIRST 1.4\,GHz flux density is at the noise level and is treated as an upper limit; as detections, these values push the fits to unrealistically low dust temperatures. The 84 radio detections have a median $q_{\rm IR}$ of 2.51, close to the assumed 2.58. SFRs averaged over 10 and 100\,Myr differ by under 2 per cent, because the model star formation histories are smooth. Without access to high-performance computing, all galaxies were fitted at $z=0$, with distance-dependent quantities rescaled. This lowers dust temperatures by a factor of about $(1+z)$ and biases stellar masses and, at $z>0.2$, attenuations, but changes dust luminosities and SFRs by only a few hundredths of a dex. These fits, with 16.3 million models per galaxy, show what UV-to-radio SED modelling can deliver on modest hardware.

papers.title: Can next generation CMB experiments discriminate between $Λ$CDM and dynamical dark energy? A Bayesian forecast for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4
papers.abstract: The combination of Planck CMB data with BAO measurements from the second data release of DESI has revealed a statistically significant preference for a time evolving dark energy equation of state parameterized in the Chevallier Polarski Linder (CPL) form. When type Ia supernovae are included, the preference reaches a significance of $4.2\sigma$ with DESY5, $3.8\sigma$ with Union3 and $2.8\sigma$ with Pantheon+. These hint at a departure from $\Lambda$CDM model. Our previous Fisher matrix analysis suggested that future CMB experiments could probe such a scenario without external low redshift data sets. Here we extend that study by performing a full Bayesian MCMC forecast for the Simons Observatory (SO) and CMB-S4 experiments, assuming as fiducial the DESI+CMB best fit in the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. We generate mock power spectra with the Cobaya mock CMB pipeline. To quantify the geometric degeneracy in the CMB between $w_0, w_a$ and the matter density, we compute for each mock the $\Lambda$CDM "shadow" model that preserves the CMB shift parameter R and produces an equivalent first acoustic peak. SO and CMB-S4 alone cannot distinguish CPL cosmology from its $\Lambda$CDM shadow since the posteriors in the $w_0, w_a$ plane remain broad and largely overlap. This is more pessimistic than our previous Fisher matrix expectation, showing that the Gaussian approximation underestimates the impact of the geometric degeneracy. Adding BAO and Pantheon$+$ supernovae data, yields $\sigma(w_0)\simeq 0.05$-$0.06$ for both experiments. However, the resulting preference for dynamical dark energy depends on the BAO data set, for instance, SDSS BAO moves the constraints close to the $\Lambda$CDM. Our results quantify the discriminating power of future CMB surveys in a Bayesian framework, and highlight the role of low redshift distance probes in establishing or rejecting a dynamical dark energy scenario.
